newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine suspends bank fx permits over hryvnya rate.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine suspends bank fx permits over hryvnya rate.

text.p: The National Bank of Ukraine will suspend four banks' currency exchange licences after they broke money trading rules prior to the introduction of the new hryvnya currency, the central bank said on Monday.
A news release said the unidentified banks and their exchange points sold the local currency at more than 10 percent higher than the official level set on the Ukraine Interbank Currency Exchange.
The central bank had ordered exchange points to keep their rates within 10 percent of the UICE rate.
The hryvnya, introduced on Monday, was fixed at 1.76 to the dollar at its debut on the Ukraine Interbank Currency Exchange.
The old currency will be removed from circulation by September 16.
Dmytro Rikberg, chief of the central bank's press service, said the banks' identities would be revealed in two days.
He also said the central bank would fine exchange points and banks not complying with the introduction of the new currency. --Yuri Kulikov, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
